about: Options whose DEFAULT changed in TypeScript 7 (most of them already changed in 6.0 (see flipped_in_basis per entry), so a project whose authoritative compiler is >= 6.0 sees no delta). Used by rule tc-03 and lib/tsgo/fit.mjs. Detection is not a text match: a key absent from the resolved tsconfig chain is `null`; the fit probe (authoritative vs native diagnostics) shows the effect, and `diagnostic_codes` attribute the extra native diagnostics to the flipped default. The source skill listed none of these (doc 08 defect 7).
applies_below_authoritative_note: Observed 2026-10-20: the same scratch config (strict/types/module/rootDir unset) produced identical diagnostics on tsc 7.0.2 and tsc 6.0.3 (TS1202, TS2591, TS2882, TS7006, TS5011) and none of them on tsc 5.9.3, so the flips arrived in 6.0.

entries.symptom: new implicit-any (TS7006/TS7031...), strictNullChecks, strictPropertyInitialization and strictFunctionTypes errors that the authoritative compiler does not report
entries.remedy: Set "strict" explicitly: true if the code base is ready (fix the new errors), or false plus individual strict flags if it is not. Explicit beats relying on either default.

entries.symptom: ambient globals from @types packages vanish: "Cannot find name 'process' / 'describe' / 'console'. Do you need to install type definitions for node?"
entries.remedy: List the ambient packages the project really uses: "types": ["node", "vitest/globals", "@cloudflare/workers-types"]. "types": ["*"] restores the old behaviour but keeps the implicit global surface.

observed.message: Cannot find name 'process'. Do you need to install type definitions for node? Try `npm i --save-dev @types/node` and then add 'node' to the types field in your tsconfig.

source: TS 7.0 announcement: `types` now defaults to `[]`, restore with `["*"]`

entries.symptom: CommonJS-only constructs fail under ES-module semantics (`import x = require()` -> TS1202, `export =` -> TS1203)
entries.remedy: Set "module" explicitly (esnext/preserve for bundled apps, nodenext for Node packages, commonjs where the output is CJS).

observed.message: Import assignment cannot be used when targeting ECMAScript modules. Consider using 'import * as ns from "mod"', 'import {a} from "mod"', 'import d from "mod"', or another module format instead.

entries.old_default: longest common directory of the input files
entries.symptom: emit layout changes (dist/src/a.js instead of dist/a.js) and TS5011 "The common source directory ... 'rootDir' setting must be explicitly set"; TS6059 when sources sit outside the tsconfig directory
entries.remedy: Set "rootDir" explicitly (usually "./src") wherever outDir/declaration output layout matters.

observed.message: The common source directory of 'tsconfig.json' is './src'. The 'rootDir' setting must be explicitly set to this or another path to adjust your output's file layout.

entries.new_default: the current stable ECMAScript version immediately preceding esnext
entries.symptom: the default lib/emit level rises, so newer built-ins type-check (fewer errors on 7) and emitted syntax is no longer downlevelled
entries.remedy: Set "target" explicitly (ES2022 for applications, ES2020 for libraries).
source: TS 7.0 announcement: `target` defaults to the current stable ECMAScript version immediately preceding `esnext`
tsc 7.0.2 TS6046 value list ends at es2025 before esnext (inferred es2025)

entries.symptom: `import "./styles.css"` without a module declaration now errors (TS2882)
entries.remedy: Add a `declare module "*.css"` shim (or the framework's client types), or set the option to false explicitly.

observed.message: Cannot find module or type declarations for side-effect import of './missing.css'.

entries.symptom: @typescript/lib-* replacement packages are no longer looked up unless the option is enabled
entries.remedy: Set "libReplacement": true if the project installs @typescript/lib-* packages.

entries.symptom: union/intersection member ORDER in diagnostics and declaration output can differ from the authoritative compiler (wording drift, not a new error); cannot be turned off
entries.remedy: Nothing to configure. Compare diagnostics by code and file (the fit probe reports wording-only differences separately); never compare .d.ts text byte for byte. On TS 6 the opt-in flag "stableTypeOrdering": true previews the 7 ordering.
entries.observed: tsc 7.0.2 accepted "stableTypeOrdering": false without any diagnostic (ignored), contrary to the announcement's 'cannot be turned off' only in that it is not rejected
source: TS 7.0 announcement: `stableTypeOrdering` is `true` by default, and cannot be turned off
